sentences.zh: 它带有天才的印记，就像拉丁字母本身一样。

sentences.en: But despite its effectiveness, Braille didn't catch on right away.
sentences.zh: 但尽管它很有效，布莱叶盲文并没有立即流行起来。

sentences.en: It wouldn't become the dominant system in France for another 30 years.
sentences.zh: 在又过了30年之后，它才成为法国的主导系统。

sentences.en: And it'd be nearly a century before it became standard for blind readers in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 而在它成为美国盲人读者的标准之前，又过了将近一个世纪。

sentences.en: Because it was effectively suppressed by a well-intentioned, world-famous visionary of blind education.
sentences.zh: 因为它是被一位好心且世界闻名的盲人教育远见者有效地压制了。

sentences.en: Around the same time that Braille was quietly developing his new reading system,
sentences.zh: 就在布莱叶默默开发他的新阅读系统的同时，

sentences.en: an American named Samuel Gridley Howe came to visit the Royal Institute in France.
sentences.zh: 一个名叫塞缪尔·格里德利·豪的美国人前来参观法国皇家研究所。

sentences.en: He was doing research in anticipation of opening the first school for the blind in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 他正在做研究，为在美国开设第一所盲人学校做准备。

sentences.en: And I wish I could tell you that while in France, Howe discovered the wonders of Braille.
sentences.zh: 我真希望我能告诉你，豪在法国期间发现了布莱叶盲文的奇妙之处。

sentences.en: But that's not how it went down.
Instead, he saw the raised letter books and he was intrigued.
sentences.zh: 相反，他看到了凸起的字母书，并且很感兴趣。

sentences.en: But in true American fashion, he found all their fancy flourishes impractical and typical of European excess.
sentences.zh: 但带有典型的美国风格，他发现所有那些华丽的花体都不切实际，是欧洲浮夸风的典型代表。

sentences.en: So he decided to make his own system that improved on the Europeans' work.
sentences.zh: 所以他决定制作自己的系统，改进欧洲人的工作。

sentences.en: And he came back and he modified it a bit.
sentences.zh: 他回来后并对其进行了一些修改。

sentences.en: That's Kim Charlson, the director of the library at the Perkins School, which Howe established in Massachusetts in 1829.
sentences.zh: 那是珀金斯学校图书馆馆长金·查尔森，该学校由豪于1829年在马萨诸塞州建立。

sentences.en: Because they were using a more Gothic-style font that he felt was a little too ornamental and more difficult to read by touch.
sentences.zh: 因为他们使用的是一种更具哥特风格的字体，他觉得这种字体有点过于繁复，用触觉阅读更加困难。

sentences.en: So if one of Aoui's French books looked sort of like an ancient tome in a horror movie, whose letters rise up in fleshy protuberances,
sentences.zh: 所以如果路易的一本法国书看起来有点像恐怖电影里的古代巨著，其字母长出了肉质的突起，

sentences.en: then Howe's system is similar, but it looks more runic, Tolkien-y, elvish.
sentences.zh: 那么豪的系统与之类似，但看起来更像卢恩字母、托尔金风格或精灵文。

sentences.en: Howe sharpened his letters' curves into points to make them more distinct under the fingertips.
sentences.zh: 豪将他字母的曲线削尖成尖角，使它们在指尖下更清晰可辨。

sentences.en: The letter O, for example, is shaped like a diamond.
sentences.zh: 例如，字母O的形状像一个钻石。

sentences.en: Howe calls his new system Boston Line Type.
sentences.zh: 豪将他的新系统命名为波士顿线体。

sentences.en: Boston Line Type is really the beginning of literacy as we know it as a movement for people who are blind in the United States.
sentences.zh: 波士顿线体确实是美国盲人识字运动的开端。

sentences.en: And like the older French system, Boston Line Type was designed to be read both by blind and sighted people.
sentences.zh: 就像较旧的法国系统一样，波士顿线体被设计成盲人和明眼人都能阅读。

sentences.en: If you're able to see and look at one of these books, the letters are totally easily legible.
sentences.zh: 如果你能看见并看着这些书中的一本，那些字母是完全容易辨认的。

sentences.en: Boston Line Type allows blind people and sighted people to sit down together and to read.
sentences.zh: 波士顿线体让盲人和明眼人能够坐在一起阅读。
他们之间没有任何障碍。

sentences.en: And this idea was really important to Howe.
sentences.zh: 这个想法对豪来说真的很重要。

sentences.en: He didn't want blind people to use a system, like Braille, that was separate from what sighted people used.
sentences.zh: 他不想让盲人使用像布莱叶盲文那样与明眼人所用系统相隔离的系统。

sentences.en: He thought it would isolate blind people and prevent them from integrating into the wider world.
sentences.zh: 他认为这会孤立盲人，阻碍他们融入更广阔的世界。

sentences.en: Long before the concept of universal design had been articulated,
sentences.zh: 早在通用设计的概念被明确提出之前，

sentences.en: it was informing Howe's thinking about how to design for people with disabilities.
sentences.zh: 它就已经指导了豪关于如何为残疾人进行设计的思考。

sentences.en: And also, you can imagine the argument,
sentences.zh: 而且，你也可以想象这样的争论：

sentences.en: Well, we want our kids that are blind or visually impaired to use the same system that our sighted kids use, right?
sentences.zh: “嗯，我们希望失明或视力受损的孩子使用我们明眼孩子使用的相同系统，对吧？”

sentences.en: But it turns out that raised letters are just not as good as Braille.
sentences.zh: 但事实证明，凸起字母就是不如布莱叶盲文好。

sentences.en: That's not intuitive to people who are sighted,
sentences.zh: 这对明眼人来说并不直观，

sentences.en: but those letter forms are just not unique enough from each other.
sentences.zh: 但那些字形彼此之间的区别不够独特。

sentences.en: Sighted people look at Braille and they go,
sentences.zh: 明眼人看着布莱叶盲文会说：

sentences.en: Oh, it all looks the same.
But under the finger, those raised dots underneath your finger are just more tangible.
sentences.zh: 但在手指下，你手指底下的那些凸起点就是更有触感。

sentences.en: And not only that, you can write in Braille.
sentences.zh: 不仅如此，你还可以用布莱叶盲文书写。

sentences.en: Unlike raised print, it doesn't require a big heavy metal printing press.
sentences.zh: 与凸印不同，它不需要大型且沉重的金属印刷机。

sentences.en: All you need is a small, simple tool called a Slayton stylus that fits in your pocket.
sentences.zh: 你所需要的只是一个可以放进口袋里的小巧简单的工具，叫做斯莱顿雪莱笔。

sentences.en: By the 1860s, some schools of the blind in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 到了19世纪60年代，美国的一些盲人学校
已经开始尝试使用布莱叶盲文。

sentences.en: And while many faculty members still resisted it as an arbitrary, impenetrable system,
sentences.zh: 尽管许多教职员工仍然将其视为一种随意的、难以理解的系统而抵制它，

sentences.en: the blind students who were exposed to Braille argued passionately for its superiority to raised letters.
sentences.zh: 但接触过布莱叶盲文的盲人学生充满激情地争辩说它比凸起字母更优越。

sentences.en: At the Missouri School for the Blind, students passed each other notes and reportedly even love letters in Braille
sentences.zh: 在密苏里盲人学校，学生们互相传纸条，据说甚至用布莱叶盲文写情书

sentences.en: since they knew their teachers wouldn't be able to read them if they got caught.
sentences.zh: 因为他们知道如果被抓到，老师也读不懂。

sentences.en: But Howe had invested a massive amount of time and resources into developing, distributing, and promoting Boston line type.
sentences.zh: 但豪在开发、分发和推广波士顿线体上投入了大量的时间和资源。

sentences.en: And he'd become a hugely influential celebrity in the field of blind education.
sentences.zh: 他成为了盲人教育领域极具影响力的名人。
他是一位出色的筹款大师。

sentences.en: And key to that fundraising apparatus was the spectacle of a deafblind girl named Laura Bridgman,
sentences.zh: 而该筹款机制的关键是一个名叫劳拉·布里奇曼的盲聋女孩的奇观，

sentences.en: who Howe taught to read using Boston line type.
sentences.zh: 豪曾教她使用波士顿线体阅读。

sentences.en: Bridgman was the first deafblind person in history to get an education,
sentences.zh: 布里奇曼是历史上第一个接受教育的盲聋人，

sentences.en: more than a full generation before Helen Keller did.
sentences.zh: 比海伦·凯勒早了足足一整代人。

sentences.en: This achievement made Laura Bridgman and Howe international stars,
sentences.zh: 这一成就使劳拉·布里奇曼和豪成为了国际明星，

sentences.en: which Howe leveraged to make Boston line type one of the dominant print mediums for the blind across the U.S.
sentences.zh: 豪利用这一点使波士顿线体成为全美盲人主要的印刷媒介之一。

sentences.en: Like Howe, many of the directors and faculty at Schools for the Blind were cited,
sentences.zh: 像豪一样，盲人学校的许多校长和教职员工都是明眼人，

sentences.en: and many of them believed that they knew which system was beSt.
sentences.zh: 他们中的许多人认为他们知道哪个系统最好。

sentences.en: Well, it's easy for me reading a print letter, so it's going to be easy for them with their fingers, you know.
sentences.zh: “好吧，我读印刷字母很容易，所以他们用手指读也会很容易，你知道的。”

sentences.en: And I think it's a failure of imagination or a failure of empathy or a failure of experience.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是想象力的失败、同理心的失败或经验的失败。

sentences.en: Catherine Kudlick directs the Paul K.
sentences.zh: 凯瑟琳·库德里克领导着旧金山州立大学的保罗·K·

sentences.en: Longmore Institute on Disability at San Francisco State,
where she's also a history professor.
sentences.zh: 她同时也是那里的历史学教授。

sentences.en: And she doesn't even really buy Howe's argument that Boston line type was universal.
sentences.zh: 她甚至并不真正接受豪关于波士顿线体是通用的这一论点。

sentences.en: You might have thought it was universal,
sentences.zh: 你可能认为它是通用的，

sentences.en: but it's universal in that way that the colonizer thinks things are universal.
sentences.zh: 但它是一种殖民者认为事物是通用的那种通用。

sentences.en: It's like, you know, these poor Native peoples need educating,
sentences.zh: 就像，你知道的，“这些可怜的原住民需要教育，

sentences.en: and we'll try to bring them up to my level and make them like me.
sentences.zh: 我们会努力把他们提升到我的水平，让他们变得像我一样。”

sentences.en: They didn't get the blind people to be the experts.
sentences.zh: 他们没有让盲人成为专家。

sentences.en: There's a crucial part is, I mean, that's like a disability rights refrain is nothing.
sentences.zh: 有一个至关重要的部分是，我的意思是，这是一个残疾人权利的副歌，没有……

sentences.en: Nothing about us without us, yeah.
sentences.zh: “没有我们的参与，不要做任何关于我们的决定”，是的。

sentences.en: In fact, the new way that people are starting to say it is nothing without us, period.
sentences.zh: 事实上，人们开始说的新方式是“没有我们，一切免谈”，句号。

sentences.en: I think Howe probably made a good faith effort to create a universal system,
sentences.zh: 我认为豪可能做出了诚实的努力来创建一个通用系统，
一个预示了通用设计的系统，

sentences.en: one that he hoped would erase the line, dividing the blind from the sighted.
sentences.zh: 一个他希望能够消除区分盲人与明眼人之界线的系统。

sentences.en: But paradoxically, in committing so strongly to the universal page of Boston line type,
sentences.zh: 但矛盾的是，由于对波士顿线体通用页面的坚定投入，

sentences.en: Howe helped delay the adoption of a much better system by close to 100 years in the U.S.,
sentences.zh: 豪帮助在美国将采用一个好得多的系统推迟了近100年，

sentences.en: a system where the blind person, Louis Braille, was the expert.
sentences.zh: 一个以盲人路易·布莱叶为专家的系统。

sentences.en: By the early 20th century, Howe had died.
There were growing numbers of organizations dedicated to serving the blind,
sentences.zh: 致力于服务盲人的组织越来越多，

sentences.en: and more and more of them were being led by blind people.
sentences.zh: 其中越来越多的组织由盲人领导。

sentences.en: In 1921, leaders from the most influential of these groups gathered in rural Iowa
sentences.zh: 1921年，这些最具影响力的集团的领导人聚集在爱荷华州乡村

sentences.en: to form the American Foundation for the Blind.
sentences.zh: 成立了美国盲人基金会。

sentences.en: The AFB quickly became the most powerful blindness organization in the U.S.,
sentences.zh: AFB迅速成为美国最强大的盲人组织，

sentences.en: and one of their first priorities was to make Braille the dominant system.
sentences.zh: 他们的首要任务之一就是让布莱叶盲文成为主导系统。

sentences.en: But, Americans being Americans, the same thing happened that had happened with Ray's letters.
sentences.zh: 但是，既然美国人还是美国人，和雷氏字母发生过的事情再次上演了。

sentences.en: We decided that we could design things better than those pretentious Europeans could.
sentences.zh: 我们决定我们可以比那些自命不凡的欧洲人设计出更好的东西。

sentences.en: So a whole cottage industry arose, with all sorts of competing systeMs.
sentences.zh: 因此，一个完整的家庭手工业兴起了，伴随着各种相互竞争的系统。

sentences.en: So, um, now we're heading into what we call the War of the Dots.
sentences.zh: 所以，嗯，现在我们正走向我们所说的“点字之战”。

sentences.en: We could spend an entire episode on the War of the Dots with Mike Hudson as our trusty narrator,
sentences.zh: 我们可以用整整一集来讲述点字之战，由迈克·哈德森担任我们信赖的旁白，

sentences.en: but in a nutshell, before Braille truly won out in the U.S.,
sentences.zh: 但简而言之，在布莱叶盲文真正在美国胜出之前，

sentences.en: there was another 50 years of competing tactile systeMs.
sentences.zh: 还有另外50年的相互竞争的触觉系统。

sentences.en: This period drove many blind readers bananas,
sentences.zh: 这段时期让许多盲人读者快要发疯了，

sentences.en: because every library for the blind was filled with books printed in these multiple competing systeMs.
sentences.zh: 因为每个盲人图书馆都塞满了用这些多种相互竞争的系统印刷的书籍。

sentences.en: New York Point, Moon Type, American Modified Braille.
sentences.zh: 纽约点字、月亮体、美国改良盲文。

sentences.en: There are others, by the way.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，还有其他的。

sentences.en: We're not going to go into them.
But, at one point, the head of the Perkins School says,
sentences.zh: 但是，有一次，珀金斯学校的校长说：

sentences.en: you know, if anybody invents another code for the blind, we want to shoot them on the spot.
sentences.zh: “你知道，如果有人为盲人发明了另一种密码，我们想当场枪毙他们。”

sentences.en: The decisive battle in the War of the Dots finally came in 1909.
sentences.zh: 点字之战中的决定性战役最终发生在1909年。

sentences.en: Cities like New York were rapidly growing,
sentences.zh: 像纽约这样的城市正在快速发展，

sentences.en: and for the first time, they had enough blind children to start building day schools for the blind.
sentences.zh: 他们第一次有了足够的盲童来建立盲人日间学校。

sentences.en: And so, they have a nice, big, two-day, knock-down, drag-out meeting of the New York Board of Education
sentences.zh: 因此，他们在纽约教育局举行了一场盛大、激烈、彻底的为期两天的会议

sentences.en: to decide which code they're going to use in the New York City schools.
sentences.zh: 来决定他们在纽约市学校里要使用哪种密码。

sentences.en: So, they bring in all the heavy hitters, okay?
sentences.zh: 所以，他们请来了所有重量级人物，好吗？

sentences.en: I mean, everybody who's anybody in blindness testifies before this body.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，盲人界所有举足轻重的人物都在这个机构面前作证。

sentences.en: And at the end, they take a big vote, and they vote for Braille, okay?
sentences.zh: 最后，他们进行了大投票，他们投票支持布莱叶盲文，好吗？

sentences.en: They say, it's the beginning of the end for the competing codes.
sentences.zh: 他们说，这是相互竞争的密码走向终结的开始。

sentences.en: By 1917, the rest of the country follows New York's lead,
sentences.zh: 到1917年，全国其他地区跟随了纽约的领导，

sentences.en: and the newly standardized English Braille becomes the main way blind children are taught to read in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 新标准化的英语布莱叶盲文成为美国盲童学习阅读的主要方式。

sentences.en: And with their increasing self-determination and literacy,
sentences.zh: 随着他们不断增强的自我决定能力和识字能力，

sentences.en: blind people are more able to integrate into society than ever before.
sentences.zh: 盲人比以往任何时候都更能融入社会。

sentences.en: Blind children are starting to be mainstreamed into public schools,
sentences.zh: 盲童开始进入公立学校随班就读，

sentences.en: and for the first time, some blind people are getting office jobs using tech like Braille typewriters
sentences.zh: 并且第一次，一些盲人开始使用像布莱叶盲文打字机这样的技术获得办公室工作，

sentences.en: so they can work alongside sighted people as equals.
sentences.zh: 这样他们就可以和明眼人一样平等地工作。

sentences.en: It's what Howe had hoped Boston Line Type would help them do.
sentences.zh: 这就是豪曾希望波士顿线体能帮助他们做到的事情。

sentences.en: But for all Braille's advantages over raised print, it didn't work for all blind people.
sentences.zh: 但尽管布莱叶盲文比凸印印刷有诸多优势，它并不适合所有盲人。

sentences.en: Like the thousands of soldiers who were coming back from war with eye injuries,
sentences.zh: 比如成千上万带着眼部受伤从战争中回来的士兵，

sentences.en: who hadn't learned Braille as kids.
sentences.zh: 他们小时候没有学过盲文。

sentences.en: And as you probably noticed, listening to me struggle to read that stupid sentence about my niece doing puzzles.
sentences.zh: 正如你可能注意到的，听着我吃力地朗读那句关于我侄女玩拼图的蠢句子。

sentences.en: My niece can ride a unicycle or do puzzles?
sentences.zh: 我侄女会骑独轮车还是会玩拼图？

sentences.en: Learning Braille as an adult is really hard.
sentences.zh: 成年后学习盲文真的很难。

sentences.en: My niece can ride a unicycle or do puzzles.
sentences.zh: 我侄女会骑独轮车或玩拼图。

sentences.en: But as sound recording became easier and more affordable,
sentences.zh: 但随着录音变得更加容易和经济实惠，

sentences.en: those people who'd become blind later in life had new options.
sentences.zh: 那些在晚年失明的人有了新的选择。

sentences.en: Options that would transform our ideas of what a book can be.
sentences.zh: 这些选择将彻底改变我们对一本书可以是什么样的看法。

sentences.en: Translating ink print books into sound might seem more straightforward than building a tactile reading system.
sentences.zh: 将印刷书翻译成声音，似乎比建立触觉阅读系统更直接。

sentences.en: After all, books were born out of a few thousand years of people telling each other stories,
sentences.zh: 毕竟，书籍诞生于几千年来人们互相讲述的故事，

sentences.en: and we all learned to read by having books read to us.
sentences.zh: 而且我们都是通过听别人读书来学会阅读的。

sentences.en: But early efforts to make recordings of books for blind readers brought with them a new set of design challenges.
sentences.zh: 但早期为盲人读者制作图书录音的努力，带来了一系列新的设计挑战。

sentences.en: The American Foundation for the Blind partnered with the Carnegie Corporation to publish experimental books on phonographic records.
sentences.zh: 美国盲人基金会与卡耐基公司合作，在留声机唱片上出版实验性读物。

sentences.en: They hired narrators and pressed the recordings onto long-playing records, 25 minutes a side.
sentences.zh: 他们聘请了旁白员，将录音压制在长效唱片上，每面播放25分钟。

sentences.en: These books were circulated by blind people about a decade before LPs became available to the wider public.
sentences.zh: 这些书在唱片向大众普及前大约十年，就在盲人群体中流传开来。

sentences.en: The first audiobooks and the first LPs were made for blind readers.
sentences.zh: 最早的有声书和最早的唱片都是为盲人读者制作的。

sentences.en: But these talking books raised big questions.
sentences.zh: 但这些有声书引发了重大的问题。

sentences.en: What should a book sound like?
